correctness.rationale: A fort containing a center must contain every leaf adjacent to that center, hence contains a proper two-leaf fort and cannot be minimal. With both centers outside, the fort condition is exactly that neither same-side leaf intersection has size one; minimality then forces a pair of leaves on one side. This gives fort hypergraph K_a disjoint union K_b. The claimed parameters and optimal-weight face follow from matching, fractional vertex cover, and vertex cover of complete graphs. Direct fort enumeration, zero-forcing simulation, and LP checks over 25 parameter pairs corroborate every step.

value.rationale: Double stars are a canonical diameter-three tree family. The theorem turns a general tree upper bound into an exact value, identifies the entire fort hypergraph and fractional optimizer face, and exhibits an asymptotic factor-two fort-cover integrality gap on structurally elementary trees. The mechanism is explicit and reusable rather than a finite isolated computation.
